html:
SMTO-GWT-0029 — Gateway is disabled

GUID: 52648e0d-003f-4449-b514-9e0a364b9a1e
Slug: gateway-disabled
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • The computer chosen for this work is switched off as a target in SMTO's Gateway list, so SMTO won't send work to it. Your request was not sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, find the computer named in the message and switch it to On. Only Gateways that are switched on can receive new work.
  2. If the switch can't be changed, point at it to read the reason shown, and ask the person who manages SMTO to switch it on. Some Gateways are controlled from SMTO's startup settings or from the other computer, not from this screen.
  3. For a new request, you can instead open the Execution target menu next to the message box, choose a computer that is switched on, and remove the disabled computer's name from your message. SMTO only uses the computers you choose and will not swap in a different one for you.
  4. Send your request again. Nothing was sent to the disabled computer, so sending again once a target is available is safe.

What success looks like

  • The computer shows On in the Gateways list (or you picked another one), and your Task starts running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. For a scheduled Task, switch its original computer back on rather than pointing the schedule at a different one.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Target selection or availability preflight found the selected or prompt-named Gateway record with enabled=false and refused to route work to it.

What this means

  • Target selection or availability preflight found an existing Gateway record with its enabled flag turned off. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Target selection or availability preflight found an existing Gateway record with its enabled flag turned off.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the selected or nickname-matched record's enabled state; a disabled target is distinct from an unreachable enabled one.

How to fix it

  • Identify the disabled Gateway named in the message. Either enable that record deliberately (enabled switch in Settings › Setup › Gateways, which is unavailable for config-sourced or outbound records) or select a different enabled Gateway for new work; saved runs and schedules keep their original Gateway and must not be retargeted silently.
  • Enable the intended Gateway deliberately or choose an available enabled target for new work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended target is deliberately enabled and resolves successfully for new work.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
